description:
A construction is sized and written once. <>, string interpolation and constant segments lower to the same construction.

Today (machine.md M5, M6, M8; compiler.md C1, C16; runtime.md R6, R7):
- Prim::MakeBitstring (prim.rs:379-427) always runs the dynamic builder: fz_bs_begin, one call per field with 6 constant arguments, then fz_bs_finalize.
- The builder is a Vec in process.bs_builder: malloc, realloc, copy out, free.
- BitWriter::write_bits writes integer fields bit by bit, so ::8 takes 8 loop turns.
- Costs:
  - <<acc::binary, x::binary>> 1667 instructions vs 376 for acc <> x
  - <<a::8, b::16, c::binary>> 1759 vs BEAM 231
  - growing <<acc::binary, x>> is quadratic: 173,841 per step; 30k appends allocate 450 MB vs 67 KB for <>
  - <<c>> of a constant byte is 528 instructions more than "A"
- Interpolation (lexer.rs:968) is a left-associated <> chain: N pieces make N-1 intermediate bitstrings.
- Exception.__inspect_indented__ appends byte by byte with <<done::binary, byte>>.

Fix:
- Compute total bits from literal widths and inline binary lengths, bump-allocate once (inline when <= 64 B), store integer fields as byte stores and binary fields with one memcpy.
- The builder remains only for unaligned or variable-width fields, writes whole bytes when it can, and keeps its buffer in the process.
- A leading acc::binary field is an append, and it is fz-nml.29's private append: its ticket 3's append_with, called with the construction's remaining fields as the fill. An unmarked accumulator with room is extended in place and the same reference returned; a marked one takes append_with's copying path. This ticket adds no second append. (The BEAM does the same with bs_create_bin's append flag.)
- <> and interpolation lower to this construction (step 8b, user ruling 2). Since nml.29 makes <> the private append, the lowering keeps it one: acc <> x becomes a construction whose leading field is acc, which is the same append_with call, so nothing nml.29 builds is undone or duplicated.
- A construction whose leading field is an append gives a small result room, as nml.29 gives a small <> result; other constructions are exact-size.
- Constant fields fold to a literal.

What goes away: bit-by-bit writes for byte widths, malloc/realloc/free per construction, the double copy in bs_finalize, per-field constant argument setup, and fz_binary_concat as a path of its own (it is append_with with one binary field). Supersedes fz-sc8.111.

Ordering: after fz-9e2.3 and after fz-nml.29's ticket 3 (the private append), which Optimize builds. The constructor form <<acc::binary, x>> is this ticket's; nml.29 covers only the <> operator (Optimize, 2026-11-18).

Asm first: targets for p03a, p05a, p05b, p06, p04a (<<rem(n,256)>>) and a 3-piece interpolation.

Acceptance:
- Constructor slopes at or below <> (bench).
- Growing constructor linear, and in place for an unmarked accumulator: <<acc::binary, x>> allocates what acc <> x allocates under nml.29's fixture.
- Interpolation allocates once per string (fixture).

Also here (from fz-9e2.2): the `unreachable!` BitSizeIr::ByteSizeOf arm in Prim::MakeBitstring (native_codegen/prim.rs) goes when a construction field carries a size type with no pinned-byte-size case.

comments.text: Optimize (2026-11-18): the fz-nml.29 page (v3) covers only the <> operator. The constructor form <<acc::binary, x>> is left to this ticket, which builds on the same append.

User agreed all four decisions on the fz-9e2 page ("1-4 agreed", in Binary Handling's session, 2026-11-18). Page: https://claude.ai/artifact/Wb77AvyLphyW8L6XmsMLL7. Ruling 2: <> lowers to the one build (step 8b). It composes with fz-nml.29, it does not replace it; nml.29's own ruling is still with the user via Optimize.

title: A construction is sized and written once; <> and interpolation lower to it
